newsitem.title: UK: Czarnikow trims India 1996/97 sugar output forecas.
newsitem.headline: Czarnikow trims India 1996/97 sugar output forecas.

text.p: Czarnikow Sugar reduced its estimate for India's 1996/97 cane sugar crop by 100,000 tonnes white value following official downward revisions, Czarnikow said in a report on Thursday.

In its latest revision to 1996/97 production forecasts, published in May, Czarnikow said its India raw value estimate of 14.24 million tonnes was based on a white value figure of 13.10 million tonnes.
It noted downward crop revisions by the Indian Sugar Mills Association and the Ministry of Agriculture.

"While there is no market significance in these adjustments to the current season's supply balance, there are concerns about the developing deficit situation which is in prospect for next season and the season after," the report said.
Policies were needed now if farmers were to be persuaded to discount their previous late payment experiences and switch land back to cane, it said.
It would still take some 15 months before new plant cane could be milled for sugar once lost cane areas were re-established.
Czarnikow also noted that this year's monsoon in India had so far been somewhat hesitant.
"It is still very early to assume a failure but the situation will need to be watched."
India produced a bumper 17.88 million tonnes of sugar raw value in 1995/96, Czarnikow data showed.
